text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes high blood pressure in the lung arteries, which strains the right side of the heart.
snippet_highlighted_words: high blood pressure in the lung arteries

text_blocks.snippet: In the early stages, PAH may cause no noticeable symptoms. As it progresses, signs often mimic other heart or lung conditions:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath (dyspnea), especially during physical exertion or routine activities like climbing stairs.
Heart palpitations or a rapid, pounding heartbeat.

text_blocks.snippet: As the right side of the heart becomes overworked or begins to fail, more severe signs can appear:

list.snippet: Swelling (edema) in the ankles, legs, feet, or abdomen.
Fainting spells (syncope), particularly during or after exertion.
Blue or gray-tinted lips and skin (cyanosis) due to low oxygen levels.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about recognizing warning signs and guidance on getting evaluated through the American Lung Association or review general overviews via the Mayo Clinic.
To help tailor this information, are you asking about:

list.snippet: Your own symptoms or someone else's?
How long these symptoms have been happening?
Whether a doctor has already ordered tests (like an echocardiogram)?
